# Migration: v2.10 → v3.0

## Summary

v3.0 is the first major structural break in this series. It ships two changes as
one release. **Work Taxonomy** replaces the ad hoc work folders with three
entities — a **feature** (`features/<slug>/feature.md`), a **work item**
(`items/<slug>.md`, or `items/<slug>/item.md` once it owns documents) and a
**cycle** — whose documents live with them, whose relationships are fields, and
whose states come from one grouped vocabulary. **Guidance Lifecycle** retires
`memory` and `lesson`, reshapes playbooks to Goal · Steps · Verification, and
seeds `docs/STYLE.md`.

This is the first migration that **moves documents you wrote**. `docs/SCHEMA.md`
§ "Who owns which file" allows a major migration to move a document and rewrite
its frontmatter and its links. It never rewrites your prose, never deletes a
document, and names every move it makes. This one does exactly that.

**What changes in your tree:** every document in `backlog/`, `fragments/`,
`investigations/`, `reports/` and `projects/` (and their `_archive/`) moves to
`features/` or `items/` with its frontmatter rewritten; the entity files a
research item or a born item needs are created; every link to a moved document —
in `docs/` and in every tracked Markdown file outside it — is respelled;
`scope:` leaves each cycle and becomes `cycle:` on its items; the owned files
(`scripts/pdocs/`, `docs/SCHEMA.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/AGENTS.md`,
`docs/CLAUDE.md`, the category READMEs) are replaced and the retired folders'
READMEs removed; the `lint` keys of `.project-docs.json` are patched in the
file's own text; the templates move to `docs/TEMPLATES/` with their seed
records, the retired ones are removed while you have not edited them,
`docs/STYLE.md` is installed, and `docs/.pdocs-seed.json` is rewritten; both
version markers move once the check passes. `memories/` and `lessons-learned/`
are kept.

The three version numbers this release moves are read by different things:

| Number                 | From → to          | What reads it                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Package and scaffold   | `8.1.0` → `9.0.0`  | `docs_version` in `docs/README.md` and `version` in `.project-docs.json` |
| `project-docs` plugin  | `3.13.0` → `4.0.0` | what you update to get the new skills                                    |
| Migration-series label | `v2.10-to-v3.0`    | the name of this guide and its script                                    |

**Behind?** This migration needs a v2.10 tree — `scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.ts`
carrying `isSeeded`. Run `v2.9-to-v2.10` first; its preflight says so if you
skip it.

## This migration is a script

One command does the whole migration. Every phase verifies itself, and any
failure stops the run with a non-zero exit and a named reason — including
failures the script did not anticipate.

**Why, in two sentences you can check yourself.** A guard computed in one shell
block and consumed in the next runs in a **different process**, so it protects
nothing. A check whose only output is an echoed string cannot fail a run. One
process and real exit codes make both impossible rather than discouraged.

## What's New

- **Features** — `features/<slug>/feature.md`, `type: feature`, states
  `backlog · ready · active · review · done · dropped`. A proposal is the
  feature.
- **Work items** — `type: item` with a UUID `id`, a `kind`
  (`task · bug · chore · research`) and the states above plus `triage`.
  `parent`, `cycle`, `scope`, `from`, `blocked_by`, `priority`, `assignee` and
  `released_in` are fields. A migrated item's `id` is minted from the time of
  the commit that first added its document (a project with no proposal: its
  latest session), so migrated ids sort in the order the work was filed; a
  document git has no history for falls back to its `generated.at` date.
- **Owned documents** — plans, sessions, reports, write-ups and artifacts live
  in their feature's or item's folder, typed by position.
- **`pdocs`** — `new item`, `new <type> --owner`, `set`, `promote`, `archive`,
  `view` (backlog, board, ready, feature, cycle, scope, unreleased) and
  `check --against <ref>`.
- **Guidance** — `docs/STYLE.md` (seeded); the playbook template is Goal · Steps
  · Verification.

## What Moved / What's Removed

| From                                              | To                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projects/<x>/` with `proposal.md`                | `features/<x>/`, `proposal.md` → `feature.md`; draft/deferred → backlog, approved → ready (active when `plan.md` is active), implemented → done, withdrawn/superseded → dropped                                             |
| `projects/<x>/` without `proposal.md`             | `items/<x>/` and a created `item.md`: `kind: task`, `done` (or `active` when its plan is), described from its latest session — with no session or plan, titled and described from the document it holds (a brief, a report) |
| `backlog/<date>-<slug>.md`                        | `items/<slug>.md`, `kind: task`; open → backlog, done → done, promoted → dropped (named for review), dropped → dropped                                                                                                      |
| `fragments/<date>-<slug>.md`                      | `items/<slug>.md`, `kind: task`; open → triage, promoted/dropped → dropped                                                                                                                                                  |
| `investigations/<date>-<slug>[-investigation].md` | `items/<slug>/write-up.md` (`type: write-up`, no lifecycle) and a created `items/<slug>/item.md` (`kind: research`; active → active, concluded → done)                                                                      |
| `reports/*.md`                                    | the `reports/` of the one research item that links to it or that it links to                                                                                                                                                |
| `cycles/*.md` `scope:`                            | removed; each backlog entry's item carries `cycle: <cycle>`; a project entry is listed in the cycle's Scope section when it is not already                                                                                  |
| `<folder>/_archive/…`                             | `items/_archive/` or `features/_archive/` when the mapped state is `done` or `dropped`; otherwise the live folder, and the run says so                                                                                      |
| `projects/TEMPLATES/*`, the report template       | `TEMPLATES/`; `PROPOSAL.template.md` → `FEATURE.template.md`                                                                                                                                                                |
| a template of yours in a retired folder           | `TEMPLATES/<its name>`, byte for byte; any seed record an earlier migration took of it by its name is dropped                                                                                                               |

A slug two documents would share keeps its date (`items/2026-01-02-fix.md`). A
document with no frontmatter — legacy archives were never linted — gets one: the
type from its new position, the title from its H1, the description from its
first sentence, `status: stable`,
`generated: { by: unknown, at: <first commit> }`; an entity found in a legacy
archive with no lifecycle is `done`.

**Removed**, and only these: the retired folders' READMEs (owned), each retired
template (`backlog/TEMPLATE.md`, `fragments/TEMPLATE.md`,
`briefs/TEMPLATES/BRIEF.template.md`, the investigation template) **while its
bytes still match what the scaffold recorded**, the `.gitkeep` placeholders of
the emptied `_archive/` folders, and the retired folders once empty. A link to a
removed README or template, or to a retired folder itself, is respelled to its
successor.

## Before you run it

The preflight lists every one of these at once and stops before anything is
written. The dry run stops on them too, so run it first to get the list.

1. **Briefs.** A brief has no successor type. Move each into its owner's
   `artifacts/` — `docs/projects/<slug>/artifacts/`, which moves with the
   project — or delete it. When you move one, also set its `type: artifact` and
   remove its `lifecycle` line (the run would do the same): left as
   `type: brief`, your own `pdocs check` reports it `WRONG TYPE` and a
   pre-commit gate refuses the commit the preflight needs. A brief that belongs
   to no project gets a project folder of its own
   (`docs/projects/<slug>/artifacts/`); with no proposal it becomes a `done`
   item, which you can set otherwise after the run. Fix the links to it either
   way: `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts backlinks <path>` lists them. The preflight
   suggests the owner when the brief links to exactly one project.
2. **Reports without one owner.** A report goes to the research item it is
   linked with: the one investigation that links to it, or the one it links to.
   When no investigation is linked with it either way — a link from any other
   document does not decide — or two are, the preflight stops on it. Do one of
   these:
   - Add a link **from the report** to the investigation it belongs to (a
     `For [the question](…)` line under its heading): a report that links to
     exactly one investigation belongs to it, whatever else links to the report.
   - Or move it into the owning project's `reports/` folder,
     `docs/projects/<slug>/reports/`, **and set its `type: artifact`**. The
     v2.10 lint types everything in a project folder but its fixed names and
     `sessions/` as an artifact, so left as `type: report` there it is
     `WRONG TYPE`, and a pre-commit gate refuses the commit the preflight needs.
     The run makes it a `report` again at its new position. Fix its inbound
     links: `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts backlinks <path>` lists them.
   - A **process report** — a docs review's status report, a project summary's
     discovery notes — is evidence for no work, and 9.0.0's skills write none:
     fold anything in it that is still true into the page or playbook it
     concerns, file a `triage` item for any finding still open, then delete it
     (and fix its inbound links).
3. **A retired template you edited**, or a file of your own in a retired folder
   that is not a document (an image, a data file). Move it out, or delete it. A
   **template of your own** — a form the scaffold never shipped, such as
   `projects/TEMPLATES/PROJECT-LEDGER.template.md` — is not a step: the run
   moves it into `docs/TEMPLATES/` as it is and names it, even when an earlier
   migration recorded it as the scaffold's by its name. The preflight stops only
   when that name is already taken in `docs/TEMPLATES/` (by the scaffold's
   templates or yours, compared without case, since macOS and Windows treat
   `plan.template.md` and `PLAN.template.md` as one file), when two of yours
   would go to one name, or when the copy is inside an `_archive/`. Rename it or
   move it out.
4. **Your memories and lessons: keep or delete.** See below.
5. **Commit or stash first.** The run leaves its changes uncommitted, and it
   stops on uncommitted edits in `docs/`, `scripts/pdocs/`, `.project-docs.json`
   and any outside file whose links it rewrites.
6. **Exclude `scripts/pdocs/` from your formatters and linters**, as for every
   migration that refreshes the owned files.
7. **Read the dry run's `yours, in an owned file` lines.** The owned files — the
   docs-root pages and the category READMEs, including the retired folders' ones
   — are replaced or removed whole. One that differs from every release of the
   scaffold holds text of yours (a convention you wrote into
   `projects/README.md`, say): the plan names it with the `git show` that
   recovers it, and the run repeats both at the end. Move what you added into a
   page of your own — a playbook, or your root `AGENTS.md` — after the run. The
   comparison ignores whitespace, table padding and emphasis marks, so a default
   Prettier run over `docs/` is not an edit. Other settings can change more than
   whitespace: `--prose-wrap never` or `always` merges a blockquote's lines, and
   a narrow `--print-width` adds a trailing comma to a YAML list. A project
   formatted that way may see an owned file it never touched named as holding
   edits. The `git show` makes that harmless: read it, and if nothing in it is
   yours, there is nothing to move.

### Your memories and lessons: keep or delete

`memory` and `lesson` are retired: nothing creates them any more.

- **Keep** (the default): do nothing. The run keeps `docs/memories/` and
  `docs/lessons-learned/` and declares them, so they stay lintable:

  ```json
  "durable": ["architecture", "specifications", "interaction-design", "playbooks", "lessons-learned", "memories"],
  "types": { "memories": "memory", "lessons-learned": "lesson" }
  ```

- **Delete**: before the run, delete the folders and their `docs/index.md`
  lines, and fix the inbound links `pdocs backlinks` names. The script never
  deletes on your behalf.
- **Fold in**: what a lesson says belongs in the playbook for that kind of work,
  as a Step and a Verification (`docs/playbooks/README.md`).

### A multi-sprint convention of your own

8.x had no shape for a project run in sprints, so some projects made one: a
sprint file per sprint in the project folder, a ledger, the rules written into
`projects/README.md` (an owned file — step 7). 9.0.0 has the shape: **one cycle
per sprint** (`bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts new cycle <slug>`), and each sprint's
work as items carrying `cycle: <that cycle>` and `parent: feature/<slug>`. When
a sprint's cycle closes, its Outcome says what carried over to the next one; an
`abandoned` cycle writes one too, saying what was falsified.

The run does not convert sprint files: they move with their project, as
artifacts. After the run, file a cycle for each sprint still worth tracking and
write its Outcome from the sprint file; a finished sprint's file can stay where
it moved. Evidence that is not Markdown — a CSV, a screenshot, a recording —
belongs in its owner's `artifacts/`, beside the reports that cite it.

### Active cycles with project scope

A feature carries no `cycle:`. The run lists each `project/<x>` entry in the
cycle's Scope section and, for an **active** cycle, says so: after the run, file
the items that carry that work with `cycle: <cycle>`.

## Run it

From the project root, with the update-project-docs skill directory as
`SKILL_DIR` in the same block:

```bash
SKILL_DIR=<the update-project-docs skill directory>
bun "$SKILL_DIR/migrations/scripts/migrate-v2.10-to-v3.0.ts" --dry-run
```

Read the plan: every move, every frontmatter rewrite, the link count, every
config key. Then run it without `--dry-run`, read the output, and commit.

The script fetches the scaffold from
`gh:ichabodcole/project-docs-scaffold-template` at the tag
`project-docs-scaffold-template-v9.0.0` — the release it was written against
(each migration runs against its own era's scaffold). To use a checkout instead
of the network, generate the scaffold at that same tag and pass it:

```bash
SKILL_DIR=<the update-project-docs skill directory>
cookiecutter gh:ichabodcole/project-docs-scaffold-template --checkout project-docs-scaffold-template-v9.0.0 --no-input -o <tmp> 'install_target=New project folder'
bun "$SKILL_DIR/migrations/scripts/migrate-v2.10-to-v3.0.ts" --dry-run --scaffold-dir <tmp>/my-project
```

`<tmp>` is an empty directory you made. `install_target=New project folder` is
load-bearing: `--no-input` otherwise takes the current-directory install. Phase
2 refuses a scaffold without the 9.0.0 layout, in both modes, before anything is
written.

### Options

| Flag                 | When you need it                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--root <path>`      | The project is not the current directory                                                                                                 |
| `--dry-run`          | Always, first: generates the scaffold, prints the plan, changes nothing                                                                  |
| `--scaffold-dir <p>` | Use a scaffold you generated (a project root, not its `docs/`). Skips the network. Alias `--scaffold`                                    |
| `--skip-format`      | The project does not use Prettier: what the run creates is not formatted                                                                 |
| `--force`            | Write over uncommitted changes in the paths the run touches — on a re-run after a stop, over edits made since the stop                   |
| `--respell <p>...`   | After the run: list the retired paths the named files spell, from the move record; `--write` to write them — see Cross-Reference Updates |

Exit codes: `0` the migration completed · `1` it could not (the reason is
printed after `STOPPED:`) · `2` bad invocation.

## What it does, phase by phase

1. **Preflight** — a v2.10 tree (config, `SCHEMA.md`, the CLI, the seed
   manifest, `isSeeded`), `bun`, `cookiecutter` unless `--scaffold-dir`, `npx`
   unless `--skip-format`; builds the whole plan read-only; **stops on every
   judgment step above**; stops on uncommitted edits it would write over; runs
   `pdocs check` under the installed CLI as the baseline.
2. **Scaffold** — generates the template at its tag into a private temp
   directory (or takes `--scaffold-dir`) and stops if it lacks the 9.0.0 layout.
3. **Plan** — prints every move, frontmatter rewrite, template move and removal,
   link count and config key. `--dry-run` stops here.
4. **Refresh** — names each owned file holding edits of yours, with the command
   that recovers it; replaces the owned files (`docs/README.md` keeps its
   `docs_version` until phase 11), installs `features/` and `items/` with their
   READMEs and `_archive/`, and removes the retired READMEs.
5. **Move** — moves every document and writes its new frontmatter; creates the
   research and born items' `item.md`. Stops if a destination exists or a move
   does not land.
6. **Links** — writes the link rewrites in files that did not move (moved files
   were written whole in phase 5), including tracked Markdown outside `docs/`
   and not in `lint.exclude`.
7. **Config** — patches `lint.workbench`, `lint.durable`, `lint.types`,
   `lint.skip` (drops `_archive`: the archive is linted now), `lint.exclude`
   (globs naming moved paths) and `lint.scopes` in the file's own text.
8. **Seeds** — moves the templates and carries their records (`renameRecord`),
   removes untouched retired templates and emptied retired folders, then gives
   every template the scaffold ships a verdict: `update`/`install` write, the
   rest are kept and named; `STYLE.md` is installed.
9. **Format, then record** — Prettier over what this run created or installed
   (never a document of yours), then `docs/.pdocs-seed.json`.
10. **Verify** — stops if any retired folder remains, then runs `pdocs check`;
    for a `MISSING FILE` the move record accounts for, suggests the link that
    reaches the document. Red stops the run here, **after** the moves and
    **before** the markers.
11. **Version markers** — both, to the scaffold's release.
12. **Cleanup** — removes the generated scaffold. Then the program re-checks its
    own invariants.

## After the script

### 1. If the run stopped, fix what it names and run the same command — do not commit first

The legacy archives were never linted, so their old broken links surface at
phase 10 (`MISSING FILE`), and a brief or report you moved by hand leaves links
to fix. The worklist is `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts report --format text`. Work it
in place, **without committing**, then run the same command again.

Read phase 10's **Suggested corrections** first. For each `MISSING FILE` whose
target this run's moves account for, it prints the link as it now reads and the
link that reaches the document:

```
docs/features/_archive/gamma/sessions/2025-12-02-old.md: ../../../../projects/_archive/alpha/proposal.md → ../../../alpha/feature.md
```

Most are links in a legacy `_archive/` that was moved into by hand, so every
relative link in it lost one folder level. The run suggests and never rewrites:
the one-level-short reading is a reading, and a link broken for another reason
can land on a real file by chance. Check each, then make the change in that
file. `pdocs report` lists the same problems without the suggestions; every
re-run of the migration prints them again, from the move record below.

The run keeps its own record inside the repository's git directory,
`.git/pdocs-migrate-v2.10-to-v3.0.json` (at the project root, as
`.pdocs-migrate-v2.10-to-v3.0.json`, when there is no git), so `git add -A`
never commits it. It holds every path the run wrote and the bytes it left there,
what it has removed so far, and — while phases 5 to 7 are writing — the plan
itself, with the bytes each planned write replaces. A re-run reads it, so:

- the migration's own uncommitted changes do not stop the preflight; only an
  edit of yours in a path the re-run would write does (an owned file, the
  config, the seed record, a template it would update, a document it moves or
  rewrites);
- a run stopped in the moves (phase 5), the link rewrite (phase 6) or the config
  patch (phase 7) is finished from the plan it recorded, not replanned from the
  half-moved tree — **but only over bytes the plan expects**. If you edited a
  document the recorded plan still has to write (a moved document, a file whose
  links it rewrites), the re-run stops and names it rather than write over your
  edit — committed or not. To keep it, copy the file aside, put back the bytes
  the plan expects (the stop prints the command for each, e.g.
  `git show HEAD:docs/backlog/<old name>.md > docs/items/<new name>.md` for a
  document phase 5 moved), re-run, then re-apply your edit. `--force` writes the
  recorded plan over it instead, and your edit is lost. A new file of yours
  inside a moved folder is not in the plan, and does not stop the re-run;
- the **move record** beside it, `.git/pdocs-migrate-v2.10-to-v3.0.moves.json`
  (at the root, dotted, without git), holds every `[from, to]` the run's links
  follow, docs-relative. It is written when a run first moves something, a
  re-run adds to it, and it is **kept** after the run: phase 10 and `--respell`
  read it. It belongs to the checkout that ran the migration — in a linked
  worktree it is under `.git/worktrees/<name>/`, and goes when the worktree does
  — so run `--respell` in that checkout, before you remove it;
- the record is removed when a run completes, and the last line counts what the
  whole migration removed, across every run.

**If the record is corrupt, or you deleted it.** A re-run without it cannot tell
the earlier run's changes from yours, and one stopped in phases 5 to 7 left
documents moved but not yet converted, which a fresh plan cannot finish. Go back
to where the migration began without losing anything, then run it from the
start:

1. `git stash push --include-untracked -m "before re-running the v3.0 migration"`
   — sets aside everything uncommitted: the migration's partial output and any
   work of yours.
2. Only if you committed during the migration:
   `git reset --hard <the commit before the first run>`. The first run printed
   it as `starting from commit <sha>`; otherwise find it with `git log`. This
   also drops commits of your own made after that commit: find them with
   `git reflog`, and re-apply them with `git cherry-pick <sha>` after step 3.
3. Delete the record, and run the migration again from the start.
4. Take back your own work from the stash. List all of it with
   `git stash show --include-untracked stash@{0}` (git 2.32 or later), or just
   the untracked part with `git show --stat 'stash@{0}^3'` — untracked files
   live in the stash's third parent, and `git stash show -p` does not list them.
   - A tracked file: `git checkout stash@{0} -- <path>`.
   - An untracked file — a draft that predated the run, or a file the migration
     created: `git checkout 'stash@{0}^3' -- <path>`.
   - **A document the migration also rewrites** (one it moves, or whose links it
     respells): do not restore the stashed copy — it is the half-migrated
     version, with `type: proposal` or old links. See your edit with
     `git diff stash@{0} -- <path>` (or against `'stash@{0}^3'` for an untracked
     file) and re-apply it by hand to the freshly migrated file.

   **Don't drop the stash until everything of yours is back.** The migration's
   partial output stays in it.

Without git, restore the tree from a backup taken before the first run, or
finish the conversion by hand. Never clean or check out the whole tree: that
also takes uncommitted work of yours that has nothing to do with the migration.
The record is written atomically, so a run that stops while saving it leaves the
previous one whole.

### 2. Run your formatter over `docs/`, if you use one

The run formats only what it created or installed. A document of yours whose
frontmatter it rewrote or synthesized is left as the run wrote it, so a
formatter's check (`prettier --check`, say) may now name it. Format `docs/`
before you commit.

### 3. Declare your scopes, and file what the run named

Add the names `scope:` may take to `lint.scopes`. File the items the run named
for active cycles, review each `promoted → dropped` item, and respell by hand
any `lint.exclude` glob the run named as left as written. If your project ran
work in sprints, file a cycle for each sprint still worth tracking: see
[A multi-sprint convention of your own](#a-multi-sprint-convention-of-your-own).

### 4. Work the "For you to check" list

Just before its last line, the run lists what it decided for you and what of
yours it replaced, gathered across every run of the migration, a stop included:

- **The items born `done`.** A project folder with no proposal becomes an item,
  `done` unless its plan was active: the run reads the work as finished, and
  cannot tell finished from stopped. Each is listed; set one that is not
  finished with `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts set item/<slug> --lifecycle backlog`.
- **Each owned file that held text of yours**, with the `git show` that recovers
  it.
- **Each template of yours** the run moved into `docs/TEMPLATES/`.

Work each line before you commit.

### 5. Commit the result

The run's record is inside `.git/`, and gone once a run completes; the move
record stays beside it, for `--respell`. Neither is ever part of the commit.

## What it cannot check

It made some choices for you, and says so in the plan (phase 3) and in the phase
5 lines. Read those lines and correct any that are wrong for your tree with
`pdocs set`:

- **An entity from a legacy archive with no lifecycle** is `done` (a fragment,
  `dropped`), and an owned document there with none is closed: a plan
  `completed`, a design resolution `resolved`, a test plan `completed`. The
  lines read `synthesized (feature, done)` and similar.
- **`promoted` becomes `dropped`**, named for review: the work it was promoted
  into is its successor.
- **Fragments and backlog items become `kind: task`.** A bug or a chore filed as
  one keeps that kind until you set it.
- **A slug two documents share keeps its date**, so an item may be named
  `items/2026-01-02-fix.md` rather than `items/fix.md`.

And it cannot check:

- **That a state was current.** State mapping is faithful: each document's
  lifecycle maps as it stands, so a stale one carries forward. A proposal left
  `implemented` while work on it is still open becomes a `done` feature; a
  backlog entry left `open` after it was finished becomes a `backlog` item.
  After the run, `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts view board` shows every state at
  once; correct one with
  `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts set feature/<slug> --lifecycle active`.
- That each brief and report went to the right owner.
- That a synthesized title or description reads well — the run takes the H1 and
  the first sentence.
- That the result is committed.

## What it does not do

- **Format your documents.** Only what it created or installed is formatted
  (After the script, step 2).
- **File items for an active cycle's features.** A feature carries no `cycle:`;
  the run lists it in the cycle's Scope section and names the cycle for you to
  file the items.
- **Delete your memories or lessons.** They are kept and declared; deleting them
  is your choice, made before the run (Before you run it).
- **Delete any document of yours.** It removes only the scaffold's own:
  untouched retired templates, the retired folders' owned READMEs, `.gitkeep`
  and `.DS_Store` files, and the retired folders once empty — and its last line
  counts each.
- **Guess at a `lint.exclude` glob** it cannot respell with certainty; it leaves
  it as written and names it.

## If you run it twice

A second run finds nothing in a retired folder, every owned file identical, the
config already patched and every template recorded, and changes no byte.

## Cross-Reference Updates

Every link to a moved document is respelled, in `docs/` and in tracked Markdown
outside it. A retired path that is not a link — a code comment, a config under
`.anthill/`, a sentence in a root `DEV_KICKOFF.md` — is not. After the run, find
the files that spell one, then have the script list what the move record
respells each to, in the files you name:

```bash
SKILL_DIR=<the update-project-docs skill directory>
grep -rlE "docs/(backlog|briefs|fragments|investigations|reports|projects)\b" --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules .
bun "$SKILL_DIR/migrations/scripts/migrate-v2.10-to-v3.0.ts" --respell src .anthill DEV_KICKOFF.md
```

Run it in the checkout that ran the migration (in a linked worktree, before you
remove the worktree): the move record lives in that checkout's git directory.
`--respell` reads only the files and folders you name (a folder: every text file
under it, without `.git/`, `.hg/`, `.svn/` or `node_modules/`), prints each hit
as `file:line: old → new`, and **writes nothing**. A path is respelled only
whole — `docs/projects/alpha` is not part of `docs/projects/alpha-two` — and a
retired folder itself goes to its successor (`docs/backlog/` → `docs/items/`). A
retired path nothing moved is listed as left as written. Read the list, drop
from the command any file you do not want changed (a changelog that records the
old layout, say), then run it again with `--write`: it writes those files and no
other. Review the diff before you commit.
